newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Colgate won't sell Kolynos for 4 years in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Colgate won't sell Kolynos for 4 years in Brazil.

text.p: U.S. Colgate-Palmolive has agreed not to use the Kolynos toothpaste brand for four years in Brazil in order to get its acquisition of a local hygiene firm fully approved, the Brazilian government's anti-trust body said.
In September, Brazil's Administrative Economic Defense Council (Cade) voted in favour of Colgate-Palmolive's $1.04 billion acquisition of the Brazilian oral hygiene firm Anakol.

But it set conditions to keep Colgate from snapping up a 77 percent market share of Brazil's toothpaste market overnight. Kolynos has around a 50 percent of Brazilian toothpaste sales and would give Colgate a 77 percent market share.

The Cade gave Colgate three alternatives: refrain from selling the Kolynos brand for four years, license it to a third party over 20 years, or sell the brand to a competitor with a less than one percent market share.
